answers.solution:
I've written and empirically verified the solution at:

**`/home/kara/SOLUTION-git-worktree-guard-missing-untracked-fixture.md`**

## Summary

**Root cause:** The gitreins guard runs the *whole* repo suite (`allow_skips=false`, `test_mode=full`). `TestROMHandling::test_rom_path_with_spaces` needs `data/rom/pokemon_red.gb`, which is gitignored and untracked — it exists only in the main checkout. `git worktree add` builds from the committed tree, so fresh wave worktrees never get it. The guard cannot whitelist the failure by design, so the worker stalls with an otherwise complete, verified patch.

**Immediate recovery (foreman-direct):**
```bash
MAIN="$(git -C "$WT" worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print substr($0,10); exit}')"
mkdir -p "$WT/data/rom"
cp -p "$MAIN/data/rom/pokemon_red.gb" "$WT/data/rom/pokemon_red.gb"
git -C "$WT" check-ignore -v -- data/rom/pokemon_red.gb   # stays clean
git -C "$WT" commit -F "$MSGFILE"                         # Tier1 green
```
Do **not** re-dispatch the worker — the staged patch was already verified.

**Prevention:** a tracked `.worktree-fixtures` manifest plus `scripts/provision_worktree_fixtures.sh`, invoked from `worktree.sh new` right after `git worktree add`. The provisioner copies only gitignored/untracked fixtures, refuses tracked or non-ignored paths, is idempotent, and preserves spaces in paths.

## Verification performed
I built a synthetic reproduction of the exact scenario (main checkout + fresh detached worktree) and ran the provisioner extracted directly from the document:
- ✅ Reproduced `FileNotFoundError` in the un-provisioned worktree
- ✅ Provisioner copies the fixture; test passes
- ✅ Second run is a no-op (`0 copied, N already present`)
- ✅ `git status --porcelain` stays empty; `git ls-files data/rom` shows only `README`
- ✅ Tracked manifest entry refused (`WARN ... is tracked`)
- ✅ Non-ignored untracked entry refused with exit 1
- ✅ Paths containing spaces (`data/rom dir with spaces/rom two.gb`) handled correctly

The final file is self-contained: symptom, root cause, exact commands, drop-in scripts, `worktree.sh` integration, and a full verification/acceptance checklist.

The fail-closed wrapper (by design) cannot whitelist this, so the worker stalls at commit with all its own verification green. FIX (foreman-direct): copy the untracked gitignored fixture from the main checkout into the worktree path (gitignored, so the commit stays clean), then re-run git commit -F <msgfile> - full Tier1 green. Prevention: wave dispatch prep for fixture-dependent repos should provision gitignored fixtures into each worktree at worktree.sh new time. Secondary lesson: the staged patch was already complete and verified, so the right recovery is a foreman-direct commit of the staged work, not a worker re-dispatch.
